The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ (A function is a relation $f$ with $(a,b) \in f$ and $(a,c) \in f$ implying $b = c$; $f : A \to B$, the value $f(a)$, domain and codomain,
> The natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$ (von Neumann)) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** Choice function and
The Axiom of Choice select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and The Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ (The power set $\mathcal{P}(x) = \{\, z : z \subseteq x \,\}$, The Cartesian product $A \times B := \{\, z \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(A \cup B)) : \exists a \in A\ \exists b \in B\ z = (a,b) \,\}$, The Axiom Schema of Separation: for each formula $\varphi$, $\forall \bar p\,\forall x\,\exists y\,\forall z\,(z \in y \leftrightarrow (z \in x \wedge \varphi(z,\bar p)))$); a natural is the set of its predecessors (On $\mathbb{N}$ the order is membership: $m < n \iff m \in n$). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ (Every nonzero natural number is a successor); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction (The principle of mathematical induction), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense (Chain in a poset). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Fix an integer $s\ge5$, a finite number $T>0$, the closed interval $J=[0,T]$, and the flat spatial torus $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$. Use the spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ and one fixed periodic symmetric-hyperbolic system as defined in [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]: its state domain $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is open, its coefficient maps $A^\mu(t,x,z),B(t,x,z)$ are smooth on the stated time, torus and state domain, each $A^\mu$ is symmetric, and $A^0$ is positive definite. The fixed-gauge Einstein state is the finite vector $z=(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi},w)$, where $p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab}$, $q_{abi}=\partial_i g_{ab}$, and $w$ is the complete matter and auxiliary state of one fixed reduction.

For the SI interpretation, the system's time parameter $t$ is the length coordinate $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ in metres, while $x^i$ are dimensionless angular coordinates on the torus. The metric components then have coordinate-dependent units: $g_{00}$ is dimensionless, $g_{0i}$ has units of metres, and $g_{ij}$ has units of square metres. Accordingly $p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab}$ has units $[g_{ab}]\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $q_{abi}=\partial_i g_{ab}$ has units $[g_{ab}]$. The model-specific components of $w$ have the fixed units declared by that reduction. Divide each component by its fixed declared unit scale before forming the Euclidean-valued state and its Sobolev norm; the resulting numerical state is dimensionless. The coefficient and source fields are those of this same fixed normalized reduction. Thus $R_z$ is a bound on that normalized state, and $R_t$ is a separate bound on its derivative with respect to the length coordinate $x^0$ (units $\mathrm m^{-1}$). Neither is a unit-independent physical observable. If physical seconds are used instead, then $\partial_{x^0}=c^{-1}\partial_{t_{\rm phys}}$; consequently the term $A^0\partial_{x^0}$ becomes $c^{-1}A^0\partial_{t_{\rm phys}}$ unless the entire equation is multiplied by $c$.

A fixed-gauge finite-slab comparison context consists of one such coefficient family on an open time interval containing $J$, one coordinate gauge and reconstruction rule, compact state sets $K_0\subset\operatorname{int}K_1\subset\operatorname{int}K_2\subset O$, separate finite nonnegative bounds $R_z,R_t$, and constants $0<a\le b<\infty$ such that

$$a|\zeta|^2\le \zeta^{\mathsf T}A^0(t,x,z)\zeta\le b|\zeta|^2$$

for every $t\in J$, $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $z\in K_2$, and $\zeta\in\mathbb R^m$. The reference state takes values in $K_0$. Compared classical states take values in $K_1$, belong to $L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$, have $\partial_tz\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$, and satisfy
$$\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t\in J}\|z(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_z,\qquad \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t\in J}\|\partial_tz(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le R_t.$$
The outer set $K_2$ supplies the positive coefficient margin for local existence restarted from data in compact subsets of $K_1$. Two states use the same chart grid, coefficient maps, gauge source functions, reconstruction rule, and fixed matter branch. Forcing terms, when included in a comparison, are continuous $H^{s-1}$-valued functions of the slab parameter; their size is controlled through the separate stated solution and time-derivative bounds when the comparison estimate is applied.

The Sobolev norms compare coordinate fields in this fixed gauge. They do not identify two arbitrary coordinate representatives by a diffeomorphism. The Einstein interpretation uses the same first-order reduction, full initial constraints, complete matter data, and local restart hypotheses throughout the finite slab.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$.

**(a) Uniqueness.** Let $J\ni0$ be an open interval and let
$u,v:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be classical solutions of
$(\star)$ in the sense of clause (d) of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], both taking values in $K$ and
satisfying $\sup_{t\in J}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, $\sup_{t\in J}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$.
If $u(0)=v(0)$, then $u=v$ on $J$.

**(b) Continuous dependence.** Let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ and let $T>0$ be a time for which the existence
theorem [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] produces solutions
from every datum with values in $K$ and norm at most $R$, with values in $K'$
and the bounds $C(1+R)$ of that theorem. Then for all such data $u_0,v_0$ with
solutions $u,v$
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'\,e^{C'|t|}\,\|u_0-v_0\|_{H^{s-1}}\qquad(|t|<T),$$
with $C'=C'(A^\mu,B,K,K',R,s)$, the fixed compact coefficient time slab containing $[-T,T]$ being included in the coefficient data.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$ be an integer, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^q)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{q-1})$ for every integer $q\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $q$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le q$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let

2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian metric $g$, density $\rho\ge0$ and future unit timelike field $u$ near an embedded copy of $\Sigma$, solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\nabla\!\cdot u=0.$$
The induced geometric and matter data are $(h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$, with $\mathcal V$ identified by $aN+X\mapsto an+i_*X$ using the future unit normal $n$. The initial surface lies in the interior of its domain of dependence; restriction to its Cauchy neighborhood gives a local Cauchy development. Every two such developments agree near $\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\rho,u$. No division by density is used, so smooth empty regions are admitted. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; no uniform noncompact slab or continuation past flow crossings is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every integer $s\ge0$, every multi-index $\alpha$ with
$|\alpha|\le s$ and every $u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every integer $r\ge0$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every integer $r\ge0$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every integer $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$\kappa>0$, let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $K$, and let smooth
complete matter initial data be given for one fixed admissible covariant coupled model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]], with the constraints satisfied and at least one development existing. The supplied local existence and uniqueness obligations must hold for that same model and for the complete data at every spacelike restart used in the proof. This includes vacuum, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic nonnegative tilted dust (with velocity prescribed through zero density) via [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]]; additional fixed models must supply the same actual obligations. Then there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of the data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
clause (a) that is maximal in the sense of clause (d) of that definition:
for every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data there is a
data-fixing development embedding $M\to M_{\mathrm{max}}$. Moreover, if
$(M'_{\mathrm{max}},g'_{\mathrm{max}},N'_{\mathrm{max}},j'_{\mathrm{max}},\psi'_{\mathrm{max}})$
is another maximal development of the same data, then there is exactly one
data-fixing isometry $M_{\mathrm{max}}\to M'_{\mathrm{max}}$; the maximal
development is thus unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry. It is
connected and, by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]],
globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

derivations.claim: Let $r=s-1$. By [F1] and compactness of $J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times K_2$, all coefficient derivatives needed below are bounded and $A^0(u)$ is uniformly symmetric positive definite; [F4] gives equivalent weighted and unweighted $H^r$ norms.

Put $w=u-v$ and $F=F_u-F_v$. Subtracting the two equations and adding and subtracting each coefficient evaluated at $u$ gives $A^0(u)\partial_tw+\sum_iA^i(u)\partial_iw=F+Q$, where $Q=-(A^0(u)-A^0(v))\partial_tv-\sum_i(A^i(u)-A^i(v))\partial_iv-B(u)+B(v)$. This is an identity: the coefficient-difference terms multiplying derivatives of $v$ and the difference of the zero-order terms are exactly the residual after the common principal operator is applied to $w$.

The composition-difference estimates in [F3], the state bound $\|v\|_{L^\infty H^s}\le R_z$, and the time-derivative bound $\|\partial_tv\|_{L^\infty H^r}\le R_t$ from [F1] imply $\|Q(t)\|_{H^r}\le C\|w(t)\|_{H^r}$. Solving the displayed difference equation for $\partial_tw$ with $(A^0(u))^{-1}$, whose operator norm is at most $a^{-1}$ by [F4], and using multiplier bounds at order $r-1$ from [F3] gives $\|\partial_tw(t)\|_{H^{r-1}}\le C(\|w(t)\|_{H^r}+\|F(t)\|_{H^{r-1}})$; here $\|\partial_iw\|_{H^{r-1}}\le\|w\|_{H^r}$.

Define $E(t)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}(D^\alpha w)^{\mathsf T}A^0(t,x,u)D^\alpha w\,dx$. Put $a=A^0(t,x,u)$, $a_i=A^i(t,x,u)$, $y_\alpha=D^\alpha w$, and $h=\partial_tw$. For $E_N:=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}\int(P_Ny_\alpha)^{\mathsf T}a(P_Ny_\alpha)$, the finite Fourier sums $P_Nw$ are $C^1$ in time by classical regularity, and differentiation gives $E_N'=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}(2\langle P_ND^\alpha h,aP_Ny_\alpha\rangle+\langle P_Ny_\alpha,\partial_ta\,P_Ny_\alpha\rangle)$. The one-order tail estimate [F10] gives $P_Ny_\alpha\to y_\alpha$ uniformly in $L^2$, since $w$ is bounded in $H^{r+1}$. Self-adjointness changes the first pairing to $\langle D^\alpha h,P_N(aP_Ny_\alpha)\rangle$. The product $ay_\alpha$ is uniformly bounded in $H^1$ by the Leibniz rule and uniform $C^1$ bound on $a$, so $\|P_N(aP_Ny_\alpha)-ay_\alpha\|_2\le\|a\|_\infty\|P_Ny_\alpha-y_\alpha\|_2+\|(P_N-I)(ay_\alpha)\|_2\to0$ uniformly on $J$. Because $D^\alpha h$ is uniformly bounded in $L^2$, the first pairings converge in $L^1(J)$; the quadratic pairings converge uniformly since $\partial_ta$ is bounded. Thus $E_N\to E$ uniformly and $E_N'\to\mathcal G$ in $L^1$, where $\mathcal G=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}(2\langle D^\alpha h,ay_\alpha\rangle+\langle y_\alpha,\partial_ta\,y_\alpha\rangle)$. Passing to the limit in $E_N(t)-E_N(t')=\int_{t'}^tE_N'$ shows $E$ is absolutely continuous and $E'=\mathcal G$ almost everywhere. Differentiating the difference equation in space is an $L^2$ identity almost everywhere because $w\in L^\infty H^{r+1}$, $h\in L^\infty H^r$, and $F+Q\in L^\infty(J;H^r)$ by steps 1.2 and 2.1; periodicity gives no boundary term.

The derivatives of $A^\mu(t,x,u)$ are bounded on the fixed compact coefficient set. The $Q$ term is bounded by [step 2.1]; the commutator terms by [F3] and the $H^{r-1}$ bound on $\partial_tw$ from that step; and the forcing pairing $\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}\langle D^\alpha w,D^\alpha F\rangle$ by $\|w\|_{H^r}\|F\|_{H^r}$. Absorbing the quadratic lower-order terms with $2xy\le x^2+y^2$ while retaining the forcing pairing in mixed form, and using [F4] for energy equivalence, gives $E'(t)\le C E(t)+C\sqrt{E(t)}\|F(t)\|_{H^r}$ and $a\|w(t)\|_{H^r}^2\le E(t)\le b\|w(t)\|_{H^r}^2$ almost everywhere. The convergence established in step 3.1 justifies all time-derivative and commutator pairings.

For $\varepsilon>0$, set $Y_\varepsilon=(E+\varepsilon)^{1/2}$. Step 4.1 gives $Y_\varepsilon'\le (C/2)Y_\varepsilon+(C/2)\|F\|_{H^r}$, hence integration yields $Y_\varepsilon(t)\le e^{Ct/2}Y_\varepsilon(0)+(C/2)\int_0^t e^{C(t-r')/2}\|F(r')\|_{H^r}\,dr'$. Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and using the energy equivalence of step 4.1 gives the stated estimate after enlarging $C$ to absorb $\sqrt{b/a}$ and $C/2$. When $F=0$, it is the homogeneous estimate.

Fix a smooth reference solution $\bar u$ with state range in $K_0$. Compactness gives a positive distance $d$ from its range to the complement of $\operatorname{int}K_1$. Put $\rho:=1+\|\bar u\|_{C(J;H^r)}$ and take initial data in an $H^s$ ball of radius at most $1$ about $\bar u(0)$, so their $H^s$ norms have a common bound $R_0:=1+\|\bar u(0)\|_{H^s}$. On any solution interval where $\|u-\bar u\|_{C(H^r)}<1$, the lower norm is at most $\rho$. The high-order energy differential inequality in [F6], integrated from the initial slice and using this lower bound, gives one finite bound $M=M(R_0,\rho,T)$ for $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$ throughout every such interval of existence; it continues to hold across uniqueness-glued restarts because the solution and its energy agree at each join. Choose $R_*>M$. Let $K_{\rm mid}$ be the closed state-space tube of radius $d/3$ about the reference range; it is compact and contained in $\operatorname{int}K_1$. Since the coefficient time interval is open and contains compact $J$, choose $\tau_0>0$ so every translate centered at $t_0\in J$ is defined on $[-\tau_0,\tau_0]$. On the resulting compact time-state set, all coefficient bounds used in the Galerkin proof of [F5] are uniform and $A^0\ge aI$. Apply that proof to each translated family $A^\mu(t_0+\sigma,x,z),B(t_0+\sigma,x,z)$ with input set $K_{\rm mid}$, output set $K_1$ and norm radius $R_*$. The common coefficient bounds, state margin and radius give one local time $\tau_*>0$, decreased if necessary so $\tau_*\le\tau_0$, and one solution bound $M_{\rm loc}$ independent of $t_0$. Smooth persistence [F6] gives smooth local solutions for the smooth restart data.

Fix the comparison constant in step 5.1 using the bounds $R_*$ and the corresponding time-derivative bound supplied by the unforced equation, [F3] and [F4]. Choose the initial $H^s$ radius so small that this estimate keeps $\|u-\bar u\|_{C(J;H^r)}<\min\{1,d/(4C_{\rm emb})\}$, where $C_{\rm emb}$ is the embedding constant from [F7]. On every partial interval of existence, a first exit from either bootstrap bound is impossible: the strict estimate persists there, the state range lies in $K_{\rm mid}$, and step 1.3 bounds the $H^s$ norm strictly below $R_*$. If a constructed interval ends before $T$, its endpoint data therefore lie in $K_{\rm mid}$ with $H^s$ norm below $R_*$. Step 1.3 supplies a restarted solution on a time interval centered there, with $H^s$ norm at most $M_{\rm loc}$; the previous and restarted solutions overlap to the left of the restart time. Uniqueness [F2], applied with the common bound $\max\{R_*,M_{\rm loc}\}$, identifies them on that overlap. The same bootstrap bounds then continue on the restarted interval. Since $\tau_*>0$ is independent of the restart point, finitely many such restarts cover $J$. This proves the claimed neighborhood.

For the fixed harmonic-gauge reduction in the geometric clause, let $H$ be its gauge residual and $E$ its Einstein residual. Define $P\subseteq[0,T]$ to consist of times at which $H=0$ and the normal Einstein constraints vanish on the whole slice $\{t\}\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. The given initial gauge condition and constraints put $0$ in $P$. At any $t_0\in P$, the reduced matter solution has conserved stress by the stated fixed-model hypotheses, so [F13] gives an open neighborhood of that entire slice on which $H=0$ and $E=0$. The torus slice is compact, hence this neighborhood contains all slices with $|t-t_0|<\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon>0$; thus $P$ is relatively open. If $t_n\in P$ converges to $t_0$, smoothness of the reduced metric, matter fields and their residuals makes $H=0$ and the normal constraint residuals zero at $t_0$, so $P$ is closed. At an endpoint use [F5] to extend the smooth reduced solution a short distance, and [F2] to identify it with the original solution on the overlap; this makes the same open-set argument valid there. Since $[0,T]$ is connected, $P=[0,T]$. The neighborhoods from [F13] therefore cover the slab, proving the original Einstein-matter equations throughout it.

The constant and the number of restarts depend on the chosen finite $T$ and the fixed compact state margin. Neither the estimate nor the restart argument is uniform as $T\to\infty$; [F11] is only an existence/maximality and isometry-uniqueness statement. The strict-fluid and dust qualifications in [F9] remain active: shocks or vacuum boundaries and dust flow crossings lie outside the corresponding local branch.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice. Fix $s\ge5$, a finite slab $J=[0,T]$ with $T>0$, a smooth periodic symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family on an open state set $O$, and a fixed-gauge comparison context with $K_0\subset\operatorname{int}K_1\subset\operatorname{int}K_2\subset O$, a uniform positive time-matrix bound on $K_2$, and the separate state and time-derivative bounds $R_z,R_t$ of [[def-gr-fx-fixed-gauge-data-topology]]. Let $u,v$ be classical solutions in that context with state range in $K_1$, each with its own source $F_u,F_v\in C(J;H^{s-1})$ in the reduced system

$$A^0(t,x,u)\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\partial_i u+B(t,x,u)=F_u,$$

and the analogous equation for $v$. Then there is a constant $C>0$, depending only on the fixed coefficient family, compact state sets, positive time-matrix margin, $R_z$, $R_t$, $s$, and $T$, such that for every $t\in[0,T]$

$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C e^{Ct}\left(\|u(0)-v(0)\|_{H^{s-1}}+\int_0^t\|F_u(r)-F_v(r)\|_{H^{s-1}}\,dr\right),$$

In particular, when both sources vanish, the finite-slab estimate holds for two solutions of the same reduced system. Fix a smooth reference solution on $J$ with state range in $K_0$ and bounded $H^s$ norm. There is an $H^s$ neighborhood of its initial value such that every smooth, admissible datum in that neighborhood has a solution of the same unforced system on all of $J$, with state range in $K_1$ and a common finite $H^s$ bound. The neighborhood size and bound may depend on the chosen slab and reference solution.

For the geometric interpretation, specialize to a fixed harmonic-gauge reduction of one covariant Einstein-matter model satisfying the complete-data initialization, smooth reconstruction, auxiliary-constraint propagation, and matter-conservation hypotheses of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]. Take the initial hypersurface to be $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric second fundamental form $K_{\rm ext}$, with $K_{\rm ext}(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Let $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ be the abstract initial normal bundle with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, and let $T_0$ be the stress tensor computed from complete matter data $d$ on that bundle. Assume the initial state is the complete initialization of $(h,K_{\rm ext},d)$, the reconstructed metric remains time-oriented Lorentzian with every $t$-slice spacelike on $J$, and the initial harmonic gauge residual $H$ vanishes. Require the exact constraints

$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK_{\rm ext})^2-|K_{\rm ext}|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK_{\rm ext}-d\operatorname{tr}_hK_{\rm ext}=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot)$$

and every auxiliary compatibility condition hold. Assume the smooth reduced solution and its matter equations and conserved stress persist on $J$ under the same fixed reconstruction and branch. Then it reconstructs to a solution of the original Einstein-matter equations throughout the slab after the fixed-gauge identifications. For a pair of constrained data sets satisfying these hypotheses separately, this conclusion applies to each member of the pair. This is a mathematical model deduction conditional on those hypotheses; it asserts no uniform collar for noncompact initial surfaces.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

In coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, a smooth curve $\gamma$ is a geodesic if and only if, throughout every parameter subinterval lying in the chart,
$$\ddot x^k+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}(x)\dot x^i\dot x^j=0\qquad(1\le k\le n),$$
with summation over repeated indices.

Let $t_0\le T$, let $u,a,b:[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $u,b\ge0$, and suppose

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t b(s)u(s)\,ds.$$

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation
$[f]\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(t)$ on smooth germs at $\gamma(t)$, extending
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] from smooth to $C^1$ curves.
Equal germ representatives agree along the curve near $t$, and the
one-variable product rule proves the derivation identity. In a chart around
$\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** For $k\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$,
a **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization with strictly positive derivative
(including one-sided endpoint derivatives), comparing the increment over the
actual image interval, are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

derivations.claim: The finite-slab estimate [F1] with zero source difference gives $\|z_n-z\|_{C(J;H^{s-1})}\to0$ from convergence of the initial data. Since $s\ge5$, [F2] gives uniform convergence in space of the metric components and their first spatial derivatives; the first-order state includes $p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}=\partial_i g_{ab}$, so those derivatives converge uniformly as well. Thus the metric components converge in $C^1$ on the compact spacetime slab.

By [F3], the Christoffel functions are formed from the metric and its first derivatives by finite sums, products and inversion of the metric matrix. The metric matrices lie in a compact subset of the nonsingular Lorentzian matrices, so the adjugate-over-determinant formula bounds their inverses; step 1.1 therefore gives $\Gamma(g_n)\to\Gamma(g)$ uniformly. The uniform $H^s$ state and time-derivative bounds in the hypotheses, together with [F2], bound all second coordinate derivatives of the metric on every compact chart neighborhood: purely spatial derivatives come from the $H^s$ bounds for $q$, and derivatives involving $x^0$ come from $\partial_t p$ and $\partial_tq$, which are bounded in $H^{s-1}$. Thus the Christoffel functions and geodesic vector fields have uniformly bounded first derivatives on a compact neighborhood of the lift set. A finite cover by convex coordinate balls, together with boundedness of the vector fields for pairs outside a common ball, gives one Lipschitz constant on the compact lift set. The geodesic vector fields $G_n(x,v)=(v,-\Gamma(g_n)(x)[v,v])$ also converge uniformly there to $G$.

Let $Y_n=(x_n,v_n)$ and $Y=(x,v)$ be the position-velocity lifts. By [F4] their chart components satisfy $\dot x=v$, $\dot v=-\Gamma(x)[v,v]$. Their integral equations and the common Lipschitz constant $L$ give $$|Y_n(\lambda)-Y(\lambda)|\le |Y_n(a)-Y(a)|+(b-a)\|G_n-G\|_\infty+L\int_a^\lambda|Y_n(r)-Y(r)|\,dr.$$ The first two terms form a constant $A_n\to0$. Apply [F5] to $u(\lambda)=|Y_n(\lambda)-Y(\lambda)|$ to get $\sup_I|Y_n-Y|\le A_n\exp(L(b-a))\to0$. Since $\dot x_n=v_n$, this is exactly $C^1$ convergence of the coordinate curves.

On the common compact phase set, the velocities are uniformly bounded. Uniform metric convergence from step 1.1 and uniform curve/velocity convergence from step 3.1 imply $$g_n(\dot\gamma_n,\dot\gamma_n)\longrightarrow g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)$$ uniformly on $I$. The limit therefore satisfies $g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)\le-\eta$; because all curves use the same time orientation, the limit remains future timelike. The uniform margin places all numbers $-g_n(\dot\gamma_n,\dot\gamma_n)$ and their limit in a bounded interval $[\eta,M]$ with $\eta>0$. The square-root function is Lipschitz on this interval, so the proper-time integrands converge uniformly. Their integrals on the finite interval converge, and [F6] identifies them with the stated proper times.
